summary: Event-frame slab for forensic SIEM ingest with signed KMS-backed manifest and delivery attestations
description: Issue summary: Customer (Citadel Health Systems, enterprise) requests a forensically verifiable 'event-frame slab' export for a 24-hour window on 2026-03-10 to support a regulatory investigation. They require per-batch RFC3161 timestamps, per-event SHA-256 checksums, and a manifest signed using their BYOK KMS key (AWS KMS key alias: alias/citadel-byoj). Impact: regulatory audit must be submitted by 2026-03-18; missing or unverifiable handoff delays compliance filing. Environment: production tenant for citadel-health (tenant id: th-04512) in us-east-1. Delivery: prefer SFTP drop to their SOC ingest (host: sftp.citadel-soc.example, username provided) with accompanying signed manifest and resume token for the attached slab. Acceptable alternatives include presigned S3 URL with time-limited access + signed manifest. Request includes sample mapping (.csv) of 10 representative events and full manifest for the slab. Support contact: security@citadel-health.example
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify tenant event range for tenant th-04512 for 2026-03-10 00:00:00 to 2026-03-10 23:59:59 UTC
2) Export event frames including full activity context, request_id, actor_id, resource_id, model_id, token_count, and redaction flags
3) Compute SHA-256 for each event payload and include as event-level header field 'x-event-sha256'
4) Group events into slab batches (max 10,000 events per file) and produce a per-batch manifest with RFC3161 timestamp signature chain
5) Sign manifest metadata with customer's BYOK key (alias/citadel-byoj) via KMS signing workflow, and produce an overall slab-level checksum
6) Deliver slabs to customer SFTP and provide confirmation envelope with resume token and delivery receipt
7) Customer verifies checksums and RFC3161 timestamps; support to provide verification steps and sample verification script

investigation_notes: Support validated tenant and found export_job_id exp-20260312-009 in export job queue; events_count matches customer sample window

S3 objects were written to internal forensic bucket with canonical naming, but initial manifest lacked RFC3161 timestamp — manifest generation step failed due to a transient time-sync error on exporter host (ntpd drift)
KMS signing call returned 400 when attempted from exporter pod due to missing grant for key alias/citadel-byoj; grant must allow Sign for the exporter service principal

Hypothesis: failure chain = clock drift -> manifest timestamp missing -> retry flow attempted KMS sign but lacked grant -> manifest unsigned. Verified that objects themselves have per-object etag but not per-event sha header yet.
